title: Agent plans: what a plan may hold, what moves it, and what a person must decide (G-360)
pins: The pure core of agent plans: the bounds a drafted plan is refused at, the refusal codes, which thread approval holds which step, how a step settles, the limits that stop a runaway driver, the reaper's stalled test, the g282.3 update and the plan context the model reads. Drift here does not error. A bound that moved would let a plan over Fancy's 8 KB contract or with a frame-breaking title reach a person's screen and the model's system prompt; a settle rule that moved would mark work done that the agent never reported or that a person refused; a reconcile rule that moved would bind a step to an approval the thread never issued; a policy that could name a plan tool would let a plan run that no person approved.
scope: PlanMachine and PlanView driven op by op with a fixed clock and fixed ids: draft bounds (step count, title, instruction, goal, markers, bidi, NUL, newline, guillemets, zero-width, 8 KB first update, shape), activation only by the proposed digest, a host call policy's refusal asked before a draft, change or approval pause is recorded (hpl-0038), one live plan, binding from pending approvals by tool and digest, decided and superseded approvals, the new-turn rule, settle and attempt/advance limits, pauses and answers, changes by kept id with compare-and-set, resume and cancel, the stalled predicate, ToolPolicy construction for every plan tool spelling, and render-time cleaning; and (G-366) the plan budget: settings validation (only per_step, shared or none, in-range whole limits, shared needs max_steps), a host choice that can lower and never raise the configured limits, the shared ledger's hold and settle (two turns never granted one remainder, an unreported cost failing a cost cap closed, an expired hold charged in full), a fixed mode, a plan blocked with plan_budget_exhausted that resume refuses, and a step held on an approval that waits while the ledger has steps left and blocks the plan once it is spent (hpl-0049), a subagent's spend inside a shared plan step settled into the plan ledger with the child's later resume holding only what is left (hpl-0050), and a child resumed outside the runner continuing its run tree's allowance, with a root that never settled charged in full (hpl-0051, hpl-0052); and which budgets a turn spends from (PlanBudget.route, the one function every language's runtime asks): a turn on a subagent child the runner did not start continues its saved run tree and plan budget whatever its prompt, an answer or a new message alike (hpl-0053), a run context the host hands a child is narrowed to what they have left, never a fresh root, while the runner's own context is not charged twice (hpl-0054), and only the plan's own turns spend from its budget, with a run tree handed to one refused (hpl-0055); and which provider/model binding a turn runs on and whether it is saved (ChildBinding.route, asked by every language's runtime): a binding a host context brings to a session that was never a child is used for that turn only and never saved, so a later plain turn runs as a root (hpl-0056), a linked child with no saved binding is refused with child_binding_missing before any request under any context but the runner's (hpl-0057), and only the runner's own context saves a binding, which then wins over any other (hpl-0058). NOT in these rows: the runtime seam (tool offer, approval gating through core HITL, the decision and run-end hooks, the plan lock, events, plan_updated run steps). Those are pinned by each language's session-API tests (AgentPlansTest.php, test/agent-plans.test.ts, tests/test_agent_plans.py). Python does not stream plan_updated steps (registered gap); PlanView.update is still pinned here for all three.
findings: Every expected value is the PHP reference's recording, and every security row was checked by hand against the G-360 design before the ports ran: the refusal code, that nothing was written, and the state a refused or superseded step ends in. Agreement across the three languages is a statement that they implement one rule, not that the rule is right. That is why the runtime guards were also probed by mutation in each language: removing the policy reservation, the approval evidence, the digest check, the report requirement, the attempt and advance limits, the compare-and-set or the text bounds turns a specific test red by assertion.
